system.name: Brannock
system.description: An Ironhull system of the middle ring: an orange star, a scorched mining world, a cloudy habitat world where most of its people live, a gas giant whose moon refines what the mines dig up, and a shipyard station where the Ironhulls weld their hulls.

owner.name: the Ironhulls
owner.what: miners (an ironhull, ironhulls; nicknamed rusters or rockheads)
owner.designLanguage: welded, modular, rusted and patched; sodium-lamp orange; hab rings bolted to rock

otherFactions: the Blackhulls: pirates, aligned with the Ironhulls
the Bloom: an organic alien hive

bodies.name: Cinder
bodies.position: the first body out from the star
bodies.looks: a rust brown world of bare rock and dust with no water and no plants: dark brown plains and crater floors, rust brown higher ground, tan ridges and crater rims, under a thin burnt orange haze

port.name: Cinder Deep
port.description: Shafts sunk into a world too close to its star. The day side cooks; the crews live and work on the night side, in tunnels that follow the ore. Ore goes up the lift to waiting tugs; food, water and spare parts come down.

bodies.name: Halde
bodies.position: the third body out from the star
bodies.looks: a water world: deep navy blue seas, olive green lowlands and cream highlands with snow on the peaks, under drifting white cloud; its sky is pale sky blue, and its settlements show warm lights at dusk

port.name: Halde Landing
port.description: The system's only real town: terraces of habitat blocks along a cold coast, a landing field cut into the cliffs above them. Most of Brannock's people live here, and most of its money changes hands in the market halls by the field.

bodies.name: Vast
bodies.position: the fourth body out from the star
bodies.looks: a gas giant banded tan and rust brown, streaked with cream storms

bodies.name: Tallow
bodies.looks: an ashen grey world of bare rock and dust with no water and no plants: ashen grey plains and crater floors, ashen grey higher ground, pale ashen grey ridges and crater rims, under a thin pale ashen grey haze

port.name: Tallow Works
port.description: Refinery towers on a grey moon, lit orange by their own flares and by Vast hanging overhead. Ore from Cinder comes in raw and leaves as metal; the air in the dome tastes of it.

bodies.name: Kettle Yard
bodies.position: the second body out from the star

port.name: Kettle Yard
port.description: A cradle of girders where the Ironhulls build and patch their hulls, welded together from whatever the last three yards left behind. Metal from Tallow comes in; ships go out.

messages.content:
You write the lore for one star system of Driftward, an Escape Velocity-style space trading game. The simulation decides; you narrate.
Rules:
- Everything you write must agree with the facts given: bodies, ports, roles, populations, what each market sells cheap and pays well for, distances. Keep each port's authored description true; you expand it, you do not contradict it.
- Write no prices, credit amounts, quantities or game rules, and no sizes, distances or travel times in units: the facts give only order and comparison. People may say what is cheap or dear at their own port, as the market facts list it, but never compare one port's prices with another's. Rumors are colour: they hint at the wider setting but promise no mission, reward or mechanic.
- Tone: grounded, worn, working-class science fiction; specific and sensory; dry humour allowed; no grand prophecy, no chosen ones. Plain prose in British English. Names should feel lived-in, not fantasy.
- The owning faction's design language shapes everything people build here.
- "vista" describes the painting on the port screen: the view from the landing field or dock, foreground to sky, matching the body's colours and the star's light, with nothing that contradicts the flight view of the body (its surface type, colours and atmosphere). Moons show their parent in the sky.
- "look" describes a person for a portrait painter: face, age, build, clothes, one telling detail; the design language shows in their clothes and gear.
- Person ids are lowercase-hyphenated and unique across the system.
